# Map to the paper {#sec-map}

| Companion chapter | Paper | Content |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 The question | §1, §1.2 | lifts, scale $\ell_q$, process $\Xi_{q,a}$, quenched laws, Theorems 1.1 and 1.3 stated |
| 2 Singular series | §1.1, §3.1, §4.2 | $S_p$, $\mathfrak S$, admissibility, $t_p$, $c_p$, $f_{\mathbf h}(q)$, criterion $d_0(\mathbf h)\mid q$ |
| 3 Prime-tuple theorem | §1.1, §1.3 | predicted count and exact integral, varying centre, Theorem 1.1, Corollary 1.2, parameters, prior work, numerical illustration |

| 5 Second moment | §2.1, §3.2 | prime-step calculation, $A_p$, $B_p$, three-moment expansion |
| 6 Divisor expansion | §3 | Lemma 3.1 (tail, second moment of $f$), Proposition 3.2 (mixed moment), Euler identity (27) |
| 7 One exceptional set | §4, Lemma 2.2 | Proposition 4.1, Lemma 4.2, prime powers (using Lemma 2.2), Lemma 4.3, proof of Theorem 1.1 |
| 8 Poisson limit theorem | §5 | reduced residues, Leung's proposition, Lemma 5.1, Proposition 5.2, Lemmas 5.3–5.4, proof of Theorem 1.3 |
| 9 Consequences | §6 | Corollaries 6.1–6.3, least prime (Corollary 1.4), prime moduli |
| 10 Scope | paragraph after Thm 1.3, Remark 5.5, §6.5 | what is not claimed |

A reasonable order for a first reading of the paper itself is: Section 1 for the statements; Section 2 for the Analytic Input, taking it on trust; Section 3.2 before Section 3.1, to see the local factors before the divisor expansion that uses them; the proof of Proposition 3.2, which is the heart; Section 4 quickly; and Section 5 with this companion's Chapter 8 at hand for the probabilistic vocabulary. -->
